fixes.new: A separate single-centre retrospective series of 120 biopsy-proven adenomas reported overall T-stage accuracy of 81.7% with 93.9% sensitivity and 45.5% specificity for the adenoma/T1 category and 50.0% sensitivity for T2, but there EUS erred mostly towards overstaging (20 overstaged, 2 understaged), and its nodal accuracy of 75.0% with N1 sensitivity 62.5% rests on only 16 operated adenocarcinomas, 3 of the 8 node-positive patients having been called N0.

fixes.old: On neuroendocrine tumours, a 14-patient single-institution series — cited here from its abstract only, since the full text was not obtained — reported R0 in all 8 pancreatoduodenectomy patients against 75% of 6 transduodenal cases with nodal involvement reaching 88% in the resection group, and concluded that the transduodenal approach may provide an inadequate oncological resection and can understage these tumours.
fixes.new: On neuroendocrine tumours, a 14-patient single-institution retrospective series reported R0 in all 8 pancreatoduodenectomy patients against 3 of the 4 transduodenal cases with a reported margin (75%), and nodal involvement in 7 of 8 (88%) after pancreatoduodenectomy against 1 of 6 after transduodenal resection, where nodes were examined in only 1 of the 6, and concluded that the transduodenal approach may provide an inadequate oncological resection and can understage these tumours.

fixes.new: Both studies are small, single-centre and retrospective, and they disagree; the 2018 paper's first author drafted the local protocol, but its 12 recipients were transplanted at UCLA.

fixes.old: The 2018 propensity-matched series on which the local protocol rests was not obtained for this revision, and the page no longer cites it as read.
fixes.new: The 2018 propensity-matched series on which the local protocol rests has now been read in full, and its abstract and results disagree on the figure most often quoted from it.

fixes.old: Its figures here come from the 2026 transplant overview's secondary report of it and from a 2026 comparison table: 5-year recurrence-free survival 42% against 44% when matched on explant pathology (p=0.45), but 28% against 61% when matched on pre-transplant characteristics (p=0.12), in 12 patients with 1-, 3- and 5-year overall survival of 75%, 54% and 42%. The direction of that asymmetry is the argument — matched on what is knowable before transplant, the mixed-tumour patients did worse — and it runs with the 2026 double-matched cohort, not against it. A previous version of this page quoted a within-series breakdown of recurrences by differentiation grade from that paper; it could not be verified from any source obtained and has been removed.
fixes.new: Matched 1:3 on explant pathology, 5-year recurrence-free survival was 42% against 44% (p=0.44; 0.45 in the abstract). Matched on pre-transplant characteristics, the results text and survival curves give 42% against 61% (p=0.17), while the abstract — and the 2026 overview that quotes it — give 28% against 61% (p=0.12); the mixed-tumour arm is the same 12 patients in both comparisons, with 1-, 3- and 5-year overall survival of 75%, 54% and 42%. Both mixed-tumour recurrence-free survival curves step from 42% to about 28% at the 60-month mark, so the paper is internally inconsistent rather than its abstract simply wrong. The direction of that asymmetry is the argument — matched on what is knowable before transplant, the mixed-tumour patients trended worse (5-year recurrence 50% against 22%, p=0.07), though no recurrence or survival comparison with matched HCC reached significance in 12 patients (within the series, differentiation separated recurrence-free survival, P = 0.001) — and it runs with the 2026 double-matched cohort, not against it. The within-series breakdown by differentiation that an earlier version quoted is confirmed by the full text: all 6 recurrences were in poorly differentiated tumours (6 of 7 recurred) and none of the 5 well or moderately differentiated tumours recurred — but differentiation was read on the explant, and pre-transplant biopsy under-graded 2 of the 4 mixed tumours biopsied.

fixes.old: the Italian multisociety guideline grades laparoscopic over open resection at low quality of evidence (C), conditional, on the strength of a Dutch nationwide comparison of 415 resections for benign tumours (59% of them adenoma) in which laparoscopy gave a shorter stay and lower morbidity after propensity matching.
fixes.new: the Italian multisociety guideline grades laparoscopic over open resection at low quality of evidence (C), conditional, on the strength of a Dutch nationwide comparison of 415 resections for benign tumours (59% of them adenoma) in which, after propensity matching, laparoscopy gave a shorter stay (median 4 against 6 days) and lower 30-day overall morbidity (12.0% against 22.4%) but no significant difference in major morbidity (4.8% against 6.4%, p = 0.78).
